items.title: Vercel for Startups: credits and FAQ
items.claim: Vercel says approved Startup Partner-affiliated, Series A-or-earlier startups that apply within 12 months of their latest funding can receive a partner-specific Flexible Commitment up to USD 30,000. The commitment lasts up to one year or until used, has a 50% AI Gateway limit, and standard billing follows after it ends.

items.title: NLnet: Apply for funding
items.claim: NLnet says individuals can apply in principle, first grants range from EUR 5,000 to EUR 50,000, and open-call deadlines fall on the third day of each odd month; its open-licence condition applies to work developed with the grant.

items.title: NLnet: Apply for a grant
items.claim: NLnet lists its next deadline as 3 November 2026 at 12:00 CET and sets the first-grant request range at EUR 5,000 to EUR 50,000.

items.title: NLnet Restack Eligibility
items.claim: Restack has no categorical exclusion of persons, gives priority to EU and Horizon Europe-associated applicants, and allows an exceptional applicant outside those areas with a clear European dimension.

items.title: Google for Startups: Pre-funded
items.claim: Google lists USD 2,000 in Cloud credits valid for 12 months for eligible Start-tier startups and states the working-MVP, 24-month founding, prior-credit, billing-account, and matching-domain-email conditions.

items.title: Google for Startups Cloud Program FAQ
items.claim: Google identifies Start as the working-MVP route and Scale as the VC-funded route; programme credits can reach USD 200,000, or USD 350,000 for Scale-tier AI startups.

items.title: Cloudflare for Startups
items.claim: Cloudflare presents USD 10,000 Tier 3 for a bootstrapped or self-funded startup under USD 1 million raised, but its general qualification list also says a startup must be funded within the last 12 months; the page does not reconcile those statements.

items.title: AWS Free Tier FAQs
items.claim: New customers can receive up to USD 200 in AWS Free Tier credits; the FAQ states USD 100 at sign-up and up to USD 100 more through qualifying exploration.

items.title: Google Cloud Free Program
items.claim: Eligible new users receive USD 300 in Welcome credit for 90 days, subject to the published prior-customer and verification rules.

items.title: Azure account options
items.claim: Azure lists USD 200 to use on Azure services within 30 days for a new Azure customer free account.

items.title: AWS Activate Credits
items.claim: AWS lists self-funded Founders credits starting at USD 1,000, up to USD 5,000 for selected participants, and a Portfolio tier up to USD 200,000 with an Activate Provider Organization ID.

items.title: How to Apply to Microsoft for Startups
items.claim: Microsoft documents a no-referral application path with USD 200 starter credits and says approved startups can unlock expanded credits up to USD 150,000.

items.title: Azure for Students offer details
items.claim: Microsoft says eligible full-time university students age 18 or older can receive USD 100 in Azure credits within 12 months without a card at sign-up; it publishes the academic-email, one-subscription, use, and exclusion conditions.

items.title: Azure free account comparison
items.claim: Microsoft presents Azure for Startups as USD 1,000 instantly for a new Azure customer and up to USD 5,000 after business verification, with 90-day initial and 180-day post-verification credit windows and pay-as-you-go after expiry or use.

items.title: GitHub Student Developer Pack terms
items.claim: GitHub says third-party Student Developer Pack offers have their own terms, may not stack, and can change or be disrupted.

items.title: AWS Activate Credits
items.claim: AWS lists a self-funded Founders route starting at USD 1,000 and up to USD 5,000 for selected participants, plus a Portfolio route up to USD 200,000 that requires an Activate Provider Organization ID. The page lists pre-Series B status, a Paid Tier Plan, a ten-year founding limit, and new-or-higher-credit conditions.

items.title: Applying for AWS Activate Credits
items.claim: AWS says Founders eligibility includes a fully functioning company website, self-funding, new-to-Activate status, and a founding date within 10 years. It says applicants hear back in 5–10 business days and that Portfolio applicants need a provider Organization ID; where applicable, the most recent funding round must be within 12 months.

items.title: Founder report: Google for Startups application evidence
items.claim: One founder describes public product and team evidence plus several rounds of follow-up during a Google application. This is an individual experience report, not an issuer term, approval guarantee, or typical decision time.
